# MIDI to MCU: Teaching the Roland MC-500mkII to Drive Your DAW

> **Stage:** Outlining — this document is the outline. On approve, it gets snapshotted to `scrapbook/outline.md` and `index.md` gets rewritten as the draft body.

**Demo video:** https://youtu.be/IIhBlliWr9k — embed in §01 or §04 (operator's call at draft time)

## Working title finalists

Pick at `/deskwork:approve` time:

1. **MIDI to MCU: Teaching the Roland MC-500mkII to Drive Your DAW** (current; specific hardware + universal "Your DAW")
2. Tape Machine for MIDI, Meet Your DAW
3. The MC-500mkII Wants to Run Your DAW
4. Hardware-First Transport: MC-500mkII → MCU → Logic / Live / LUNA

## Dek (one sentence)

A bridge service that translates MIDI Song Position Pointer + transport from the Roland MC-500mkII (1988 · 8-track · Super MRC OS) into Mackie Control Universal — turning the MC-500's panel into a tactile transport controller for any MCU-compatible DAW.

## Section structure

Seven sections. Magazine dividers (`---`) between. Sentence-case headings. 3–6 bolded lead-ins clustered in §03 ("What's tested") and §07 ("Lessons / what actually works").

### § 01 — The hard problem (one paragraph)

State plainly: the MC-500mkII is a multitrack tape machine for MIDI. It has good buttons. It does not, by itself, talk to your DAW.

Frame the bridge in one sentence as the closing of that gap. **Don't** open with a marketing-style hook — drop straight into the spec.

### § 02 — What it is

Bridge process on the laptop. Opens a CoreMIDI virtual port; listens to the MC-500mkII over MIDI; emits MCU to the DAW.

ASCII diagram:

```
MC-500mkII  →  bridge  →  MCU  →  DAW
   (MIDI)              (CoreMIDI virtual port)
```

Optional: embed the demo video (https://youtu.be/IIhBlliWr9k) here as the worked example. Reads more naturally than embedding under §04 because §02 is where the reader first learns *what the thing does*.

### § 03 — What's tested

Three bolded lead-ins. Service-manual-style enumerated findings:

- **Hardware.** MC-500mkII · 1988 · 8-track · Super MRC OS. The Super MRC OS is the load-bearing requirement — the original 1986 MC-500 lacks it. The Roland MC-50 (1989, smaller, similar architecture) probably works, untested.
- **DAWs.** Logic Pro, Ableton Live, LUNA. MCU is universal in theory; only three claimed because only three have been run end-to-end.
- **Platform.** macOS via CoreMIDI. Linux/ALSA compiles and runs but hasn't been put against a real DAW. No Windows build yet.

### § 04 — What you get from the panel

Transport one-for-one (stop, play, record, FF, RW). Data wheel = jog wheel; fine resolution slow, faster scrub when you spin.

Location memories are the interesting part: 99 markers in NVRAM map to MCU `LOCATE` messages. Pre-configure the verse / chorus / bridge of a session as MC-500 locations; the panel becomes a tactile arrangement-jumping interface for whatever DAW is on the other end.

If demo video isn't in §02, embed it here — this is the section the reader most wants to *see* working.

### § 05 — How it works

Brief technical:

- SPP → 14-bit MIDI beat positions @ 1/16-note resolution
- Bridge converts SPP → MTC at session sample rate
- Wraps position in MCU `GOTO`; DAW seeks
- Start/stop/continue map directly to MCU transport
- Jog wheel CC → MCU jog deltas scaled to the DAW's frame rate
- The CoreMIDI virtual port is what the DAW connects to as an MCU surface — no driver, no kernel extension, no DAW plugin

Two paragraphs max. The dispatch isn't a protocol spec; it's a worked-example intro.

### § 06 — Get it

Distribution channels:

- Pre-compiled binaries for macOS and Linux
- Homebrew formula
- macOS `.app` — drag into `/Applications/`, no terminal required

→ Releases: <https://github.com/audiocontrol-org/audiocontrol/releases>
→ Source: <https://github.com/audiocontrol-org/audiocontrol>

### § 07 — What's next

Brief, honest:

- MC-50 verification (similar architecture, untested)
- Windows binaries
- More MCU surface — channel select, v-pots

Close with: *"If you have an MC-500mkII and a DAW, try it. If it breaks on your setup, file an issue with the platform and DAW version."*
